observations: A treadle (manual, foot-pedal) sewing machine mounted in a wooden cabinet/table with a fold-up top.
Machine head is cream/white enamel with chrome knobs; visible paint chipping and orange rust spots on the body (clearly seen in photo 1 and photo 3).
Brand name 'MERCURY' is readable on the machine's front plate in photo 1 and photo 2.
The cast-iron treadle base has a metal grille stamped 'SUPREME' (visible in photo 2 and photo 3).
Wooden cabinet is maroon/reddish with two side drawers; surface looks intact but corners/joints are not shown closely.
No power cord, plug, or motor is visible anywhere — this appears to be a purely manual treadle machine, not electrified.
No fabric, thread, or stitching sample is shown to demonstrate the machine actually sews.
Background shows an outdoor roadside setting with an advert board ('Quick Charge Spot'), consistent with a casual resale photo, not a studio or shop listing.

identity.kind: treadle sewing machine with wooden cabinet

claims.evidence: Photo 1 and photo 3 show paint flaking and rust spots on the machine body, which is not consistent with 'perfect condition'.

risks.risk: Whether the machine actually sews (stitch formation, tension, bobbin mechanism working)
risks.proof: A short video of the treadle being pedaled and a test seam being sewn on fabric

risks.risk: Condition of the belt connecting the treadle wheel to the machine head (missing, cracked, or loose)
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the belt and wheel connection

risks.risk: Internal rust or seizure affecting moving parts (needle bar, shuttle, gears)
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the needle plate area and underside mechanism
risks.if_unproven: priced as having moderate-to-heavy surface rust risk

risks.risk: Structural integrity of the wooden cabinet (cracks, loose joints, drawer function)
risks.proof: Close-up of drawer fully opened and of the leg/table joints
risks.if_unproven: priced as cosmetic condition only, structure unverified

risks.risk: Completeness of accessories (bobbins, needles, extra attachments)
risks.proof: Photo of included accessories laid out
risks.if_unproven: priced as bare machine with no accessories

proof_requests: Video of the treadle being operated and a test stitch being sewn on fabric
Close-up of the belt and wheel linkage
Close-up of the underside/bobbin area for rust or wear
Photo of drawers opened and table joints
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable as a Mercury-brand treadle sewing machine in a wooden cabinet, but visible rust and paint damage contradict the seller's 'perfect condition' claim, and no functional proof (stitching, belt, mechanism) is shown, so it must be priced at worst case as a non-verified, cosmetically worn, non-demonstrated-working unit.
